description: Studio-wide Renovate base preset (igonzalezespi). Every consumer repo's renovate.json extends `github>igonzalezespi-apps/renovate-config`. Dependency PRs target `develop`, Conventional `chore(deps)` commits. Repo-specific version-holds and overrides live in each repo's own renovate.json and are merged on top of this one.

SINGLE-WRITER MODEL (2026-08-02): GitHub *detects* (Dependency graph + Dependabot alerts, enabled per repo via `PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/vulnerability-alerts`), Renovate is the *only* bot that opens PRs. Dependabot security updates (`automated-security-fixes`) stay OFF and no repo carries a `.github/dependabot.yml`. Renovate NEEDS those alerts for `vulnerabilityAlerts` to fire — it consumes them and opens the PRs itself. Two bots writing the same manifests produce duplicate PRs per CVE, cross-branch lockfile conflicts and competing automerges. See README.md.

Supply chain (2026-08-02): `minimumReleaseAge` holds every ordinary dependency PR for a 7-day cooldown, so a version that is yanked or found malicious in its first days never reaches a repo. It is the cheap defence against the compromised-release pattern (a package publishing a malicious version that is pulled hours later). `internalChecksFilter: strict` withholds the PR until the cooldown is met instead of opening it pending.

The cooldown is overridden back to `minimumReleaseAge: null` inside `vulnerabilityAlerts` ON PURPOSE — it is Renovate's default there, and stated explicitly so nobody 'tidies it away': a fix for a known CVE must not wait out the cooldown, which would invert the control into a delay on exactly the update that must land fastest. Those PRs also get `prCreation: immediate` and bypass the rate limits. `osvVulnerabilityAlerts` adds the OSV feed, which covers DIRECT dependencies only — it complements the GitHub alerts, it does not replace them.

Transitive dependencies are covered by `lockFileMaintenance`, not by the ordinary PRs (those bump direct deps). Its schedule is a cron window spanning the whole of Tuesday: the legacy `later` syntax reads well but a narrow window risks the bot run never landing inside it, and a PR that is never created cannot automerge. `prPriority` for it lives in packageRules — Renovate rejects it inside `lockFileMaintenance`.

`lockFileMaintenance` sets `minimumReleaseAge: null` ON PURPOSE, and it is the second exemption in this file for the same structural reason as `vulnerabilityAlerts`: the cooldown and the job’s own purpose cannot both hold. Lockfile maintenance exists to refresh the WHOLE transitive tree to its newest resolutions; a 7-day floor forbids exactly that, so `renovate/stability-days` goes to `pending` on every regeneration and never clears. Measured 2026-08-16 on two of the maintainer’s other repos: their open lockfile-maintenance PRs, opened on 08-06 and 08-10, had been pending for 10 and 6 days, and the timestamps close the case — the branch was regenerated at 08:39:00 and the check went pending at 08:39:04, every single run.

Read the trade honestly, because it IS a weakening: with the floor in place the fleet got NEITHER side of the deal — the PRs never went green, so they never automerged, so transitive dependencies never updated at all, while the cooldown protected nothing that was landing, because nothing was. The floor stays where it does its job: ordinary PRs, which bump the DIRECT dependencies a human chose. What is now uncovered is a compromised TRANSITIVE release in its first days. If that trade is unwanted, the alternative is not restoring the floor here — it is disabling `lockFileMaintenance` outright, because with the floor on that is its effective state anyway, only noisier.

Automerge (decision 2026-08-02, superseding the 2026-06-05 'only Ivan merges' posture): patch/pin/digest and lockFileMaintenance merge themselves once checks are green. Majors, and minors of 0.x packages, are gated behind a Dependency Dashboard tick. `automergeStrategy: squash` matches the studio rule that bot PRs land squashed; a repo whose settings disallow squash overrides it in its own renovate.json.

Each PR is auto-labelled with exactly one `semver:major|minor|patch` by update type (2026-06-09) so the release-mechanism's require-semver-label gate passes on bot PRs and the develop->main version bump is computed correctly from merged dependency PRs.

`toolSettings.nodeMaxMemory` (2026-08-02): the largest consumer repo was running OUT OF MEMORY during Renovate's lockfile refresh. Renovate shells out to the package manager to regenerate a lockfile, and by default that child Node process 'automagically determines' its own heap limit; a large pnpm workspace exceeds it and the run dies. The failure mode is SILENCE — a run that dies mid-lockfile produces no PR, so the bot looks like it has nothing to say, which is indistinguishable from everything being up to date. Value is in MiB (2048 = 2 GiB), matching the setting already proven on the downstream repo that hit this first. It applies to the `npm` manager family only (npm/yarn/pnpm) — it is read in the npm post-update path, including the pnpm one — so in a Flutter/Gradle repo the equivalent knob is `toolSettings.jvmMaxMemory`, not this. Set fleet-wide from here rather than per repo: the repo that needs it today is not the one that will need it next, and a per-repo fix has to be rediscovered every time. Repo-level option, verified against the shipped option definitions: it carries no `globalOnly` flag, and its own description says global self-hosted config merely takes precedence — so the hosted app honours it.

`minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour: timestamp-optional` for `docker` (2026-08-18): the THIRD exemption to the cooldown in this file, and the only one that was never a choice. Renovate's docker datasource reads release timestamps from the Docker Hub API alone; a plain registry — MCR, GHCR, Quay, ECR — exposes none (renovate#38656 is the open feature request, and the docs table for minimum-release-age carries the row `docker | (not Docker Hub) | no`). Since v42 the default `minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour` is `timestamp-required`, which reads "no timestamp" as "not old enough". That timestamp is never going to arrive, so for those registries the 7-day cooldown above stops being a delay and becomes a PERMANENT block — and `internalChecksFilter: strict` withholds the update from the dashboard too, so there is no warning, no pending section, nothing to look at. Measured on a consumer repo with `LOG_LEVEL=debug renovate --platform=local --dry-run=lookup`, rolling its Playwright container image back one version so a candidate existed: the debug log marked all four newer releases pending for a missing releaseTimestamp and the update carried `pendingChecks: true`; with this rule that line is gone and the update is emitted, into the same branch and with the digest resolved. It had already cost eight days of that image sitting behind its npm runner until a human bumped it by hand. Read the scope precisely, because it is narrower than it looks: `matchDatasources: ["docker"]` with no package filter does NOT blanket-disable the cooldown — a release that DOES carry a timestamp (everything from Docker Hub) still serves the full 7 days. What it gives up, said plainly: an image from a timestamp-less registry now lands with no age gate at all.

`matchDepTypes: ["packageManager"] / enabled: false` (2026-08-18): hoisted from three consumer repos that each carried it verbatim. Renovate rewrites `pnpm@X.Y.Z+sha512…` down to `pnpm@X.Y.Z` and DROPS the corepack integrity hash, so the pin stops being verifiable; a `setup-repo` that fails closed on a hashless pin then breaks CI, and one that does not just installs an unverified package manager. Bump pnpm on purpose with `corepack use pnpm@<version>`, which writes the hash back. It lives here rather than per repo because the exposure follows the FIELD, not the repo: measured on 2026-08-18, one of the public config repos already carries `packageManager: pnpm@11.17.0+sha512…` with no hold of its own — the gap was open there and simply had not been hit yet. Repos without the field (Flutter, and the ones with no package.json) are unaffected: the depType never matches.

packageRules.description: Patch-class updates: automerge once checks are green + label semver:patch for the release-mechanism gate
Minor updates: human review + label semver:minor
Major updates: gated behind a Dependency Dashboard tick, then human review + label semver:major
Pre-1.0 packages treat a minor as breaking, so gate 0.x minors behind the dashboard as well
Lock-file maintenance keeps the transitive tree current, so it jumps the queue ahead of the ordinary updates. Label semver:patch (a relock is a patch-class change for the release gate).

Docker releases outside Docker Hub carry no timestamp, so timestamp-required (the v42+ default) turns the cooldown into a permanent, silent block. Timestamped releases are unaffected and still serve the full minimumReleaseAge.
Group GitHub Actions and keep them pinned to SHA
Group non-major npm updates into one PR
HOLD pnpm majors: pnpm 10 is the deliberate studio standard; majors are a coordinated decision, never an automatic dependency PR. Bump it studio-wide on purpose, not because Renovate opened a PR.
HOLD typescript majors: TS majors land studio-wide together with @studio/tsconfig peers (Wave D), not piecemeal per repo. Hold the automatic PR; the major is a coordinated rollout.
HOLD the packageManager field: Renovate drops the corepack integrity hash when it rewrites the pin, leaving it unverifiable. Bump pnpm with `corepack use pnpm@<version>`, which writes the hash back.
